headline: Computational tools resolve noise and spatial context in single-cell and spatial omics
label: Single Cell Computational Methods
summary: Single-cell and spatial datasets now support stage-specific models of regulation, cell fate, disease risk and tissue architecture.
synthesis: The dominant thread is explicit computational handling of a specific noisy or ambiguous step in single-cell and spatial data. SEBULA models snATAC-seq multiplets with FDR control, scATS corrects RNA degradation bias to quantify alternative transcription start sites per cell, and the Xenium study characterizes sensitivity and signal contamination before introducing SPLIT. Spatial tools address segmentation (TENGU), copy number detection (SpaCNA) and motif discovery (SpatialQuery). A second thread is in silico perturbation: CellxPert and the islet digital twin both enable computational perturbation, with the latter validating STAT1 and ZEB1 regulators. Across these items, each tool targets one analytical stage rather than a unified pipeline. Several items, including PFM and PICDGI, instead model dynamic regulatory interactions and do not fit the noise-correction thread.
